quarterly_data.signal: FY2026 (fiscal year ended March 31, 2026) consolidated results: revenue JPY 3,356,969 million (+5.0% YoY), growing mainly in Bio CDMO, semiconductor materials and imaging; operating income JPY 350,210 million (+6.1%); income before income taxes JPY 366,629 million (+7.6%); net income attributable to shareholders JPY 276,735 million (+6.0%). The company states revenue set a record for the 4th consecutive year, operating income for the 5th and net income for the 6th. Domestic revenue JPY 1,168,682 million (+6.3%), overseas revenue JPY 2,188,287 million (+4.4%); actual exchange rates JPY 151 per US dollar and JPY 175 per euro.
quarterly_data.figure: Revenue JPY 3,356,969 million (+5.0%); operating income JPY 350,210 million (+6.1%); net income JPY 276,735 million (+6.0%)

quarterly_data.signal: Electronics segment FY2026: revenue JPY 456,157 million (+11.9%), up on higher sales in the semiconductor materials and display materials businesses; operating income JPY 100,883 million (+34.4%), driven mainly by higher sales of semiconductor materials for generative AI. Management states the semiconductor materials business steadily captured AI-semiconductor demand and its sales rose significantly: sales to major foundries stayed strong and sales to major US and Korean semiconductor makers are recovering. By product, advanced resists, NTI (negative tone imaging) developer and copper-wiring CMP slurry (both described by the company as world's top share) grew with miniaturization and the rising number of wiring layers; in back-end materials, sales of liquid polyimide for interlayer dielectric films used for chip-to-chip connection grew with advanced-packaging demand for AI semiconductors. The AF (advanced functional) materials business grew on adoption of new display materials and strong sales of resist materials for semiconductors. (From FY2026, chemical reagents moved from the Electronics to the Healthcare segment; prior-year figures restated.)
quarterly_data.figure: Electronics revenue JPY 456,157 million (+11.9%); operating income JPY 100,883 million (+34.4%)

quarterly_data.signal: Other segments FY2026: Healthcare revenue JPY 1,098,925 million (+4.9%, led by Medical Systems and Bio CDMO), operating income JPY 63,637 million (-20.3%) hurt by exchange rates and higher raw-material costs from the surge in silver prices; Business Innovation revenue JPY 1,174,800 million (-2.0%) on weak markets and cutting low-margin models, operating income JPY 63,712 million (-14.6%) also hit by one-time Asia-Pacific restructuring costs; Imaging revenue JPY 627,087 million (+15.7%), operating income JPY 160,003 million (+14.9%) on strong instax instant photo system (cumulative sales above 100 million units) and digital camera sales.

quarterly_data.signal: Company forecast for FY2027 (the year ending March 2027; the company's 'fiscal 2026'): revenue JPY 3,470 billion (+3.4%), operating income JPY 365 billion (+4.2%), income before income taxes JPY 375 billion (+2.3%), net income attributable to shareholders JPY 280 billion (+1.2%), ROE 7.8%, ROIC 5.6%, assuming JPY 150 per US dollar and JPY 175 per euro. The VISION2030 medium-term plan's targets for the same year are revenue JPY 3,450 billion, operating income JPY 360 billion, net income JPY 270 billion, ROE 8.1% and ROIC 5.8%. Management states it will accelerate growth of the Healthcare and Electronics segments, and the Healthcare segment aims for revenue above JPY 1 trillion again with further growth.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2027 forecast: revenue JPY 3,470 billion (+3.4%); operating income JPY 365 billion (+4.2%); net income JPY 280 billion (+1.2%)

quarterly_data.signal: Management states demand for semiconductors keeps expanding, centred on AI semiconductors, and expects higher integration in back-end processes to accelerate alongside miniaturization; the semiconductor materials business, which supplies materials to almost every chip-manufacturing process, will accelerate growth by offering 'one-stop solutions' to complex customer problems no single material can solve. It stresses local production, local consumption and local support, investing actively in sites in Japan, the US, Europe and Asia, which management says also reduces geopolitical supply-chain risk; in India it has acquired land for a manufacturing site as it prepares to enter that market. In photoresists, a focus product, it presented its latest advanced resist technology centred on next-generation EUV at SPIE Advanced Lithography + Patterning 2026 (February 2026) and in April 2026 announced development of a fluorine-free resist for negative-tone ArF immersion, which it calls the world's first; management says customers rate these EUV and ArF technologies highly and inquiries are steadily increasing.

Back-end materials: management expects demand for film-type polyimide to rise as interposers become larger and build-up substrates finer, and CMP slurry that planarizes with high precision in advanced-packaging steps such as hybrid bonding is being evaluated for applications. Several advanced-packaging customers have high expectations for these materials, full-scale sample evaluations have started and work toward adoption is expanding. The company has started selling a CMP slurry for advanced packaging that is adopted by a major semiconductor device maker as an essential slurry for planarizing the bonding surfaces in hybrid bonding.

R&D (semiconductor materials): the company says it developed the world's first fluorine-free negative-tone ArF immersion photoresist (no fluorine-containing raw materials), for the advanced nodes used to make AI semiconductors, with high acid-reaction efficiency and water repellency that reduces water residue in immersion exposure; it aims to start selling it early after customer evaluations. It earlier developed the world's first NTI developer using high-purity organic solvent, sells a PFAS-free nanoimprint resist and developed a PFAS-free negative-tone ArF immersion resist. A new development and evaluation building at Fujifilm Electronic Materials' Shizuoka plant was completed and began operating in November 2025, to speed up new materials for advanced and next-generation semiconductors, keep high-quality supply stable and meet rising demand for semiconductors for AI data centers. The company says its line-up covers almost the whole chip-manufacturing process from the leading edge to legacy nodes, with production sites in major countries of Japan, the US, Europe and Asia.

AF materials: launched the FUJIFILM LTO Ultrium 10 (40TB) data cartridge in January 2026, with up to 100TB per cartridge (40TB uncompressed), the largest capacity in the series, using the company's fine-particle hybrid magnetic material and a new thinning technology that lengthens the tape. Management also plans to expand supply of data tape for the data centers being built worldwide as storage demand grows, Prescale pressure-measuring film for semiconductor and display manufacturing, and polymers and photoacid generators for semiconductor materials.

Customer Rapidus: in February 2026 Fujifilm completed a JPY 5 billion investment in Rapidus, which aims to mass-produce leading-edge logic semiconductors. The company states it will strongly support Rapidus' development and manufacturing of leading-edge semiconductors by providing a broad range of semiconductor materials and technologies, and will accelerate development of materials for next-generation semiconductors by working closely with Rapidus on next-generation process development.
quarterly_data.figure: JPY 5 billion investment in Rapidus (completed February 2026)

quarterly_data.signal: Bio CDMO capacity: FUJIFILM Biotechnologies opened its large biopharmaceutical plant in North Carolina (US; opening ceremony September 2025) and the first-phase 8 x 20,000-liter mammalian cell culture tanks are in full operation; 8 more tanks of the same size will be added in 2028, which the company says (its own research) will give it one of the largest drug-substance capacities of any bio CDMO site in North America. Long-term manufacturing contracts have been signed for the North Carolina site with Janssen Supply Group, LLC (Johnson & Johnson group) and Regeneron, and management is bringing forward the start of the site's second-phase investment on rising US manufacturing demand, with FY2027 (the year ending March 2027; the company's 'fiscal 2026') still an up-front investment period. In the UK, an antibody drug-substance building and process development lab (about GBP 400 million investment) opened in February 2026. In Toyama (Japan), one of Japan's largest biopharmaceutical CDMO plants was completed in 2025 and is planned to operate from FY2028 (the year ending March 2028; the company's 'fiscal 2027') (antibodies and ADCs normally; mRNA and recombinant-protein vaccines in a pandemic).
quarterly_data.figure: 8 x 20,000-liter tanks running in North Carolina; 8 more tanks of the same size in 2028

quarterly_data.signal: Customer Regeneron: in April 2025 FUJIFILM Biotechnologies signed a biopharmaceutical manufacturing agreement with Regeneron Pharmaceuticals worth more than US$3 billion in total, under which it will manufacture Regeneron's antibody drugs for 10 years.
quarterly_data.figure: More than US$3 billion; 10-year manufacturing agreement

quarterly_data.signal: Customer argenx: in September 2025 FUJIFILM Biotechnologies signed a new agreement with argenx, an immunology-focused biopharmaceutical company, to manufacture the drug substance of argenx's efgartigimod.
